meta.title: That Store Card Discount Costs More Than It Saves
meta.hook: That store card offering 20% off today's purchase can charge over 30% interest for years after.
meta.description: Retail store credit cards routinely carry some of the highest interest rates in the card industry — often north of 30% APR versus roughly 21% for general-purpose cards, per Bankrate's annual retail card survey. The one-time discount is real; so is the interest, and it outlasts the discount if a balance is carried.

scenes.narration: That store card offering twenty percent off today's purchase can charge you more than thirty percent interest for years after.

visual.query: cashier offering store credit card signup checkout
visual.visual_intent: A checkout counter moment with a card being offered at the register, warm retail light, close on hands
visual.decision_reason: hook beat: the tempting offer, hard cut

scenes.narration: Retail credit cards routinely carry some of the highest interest rates in the entire card industry.

visual.visual_intent: A row of retail storefronts in a shopping center, daylight, wide establishing shot

scenes.narration: General-purpose credit cards average interest in the low twenties. Store-only cards average well over thirty percent.

visual.query: two bar chart columns comparing percentages screen
visual.visual_intent: Two glowing bar columns on a dark financial screen, one clearly taller than the other, teal and gold
visual.decision_reason: Bankrate 2025 retail credit card survey: retail ~30%+ APR vs general-purpose ~21% average

scenes.narration: That gap exists because store cards are underwritten differently. Approval is easy. The bank is pricing in default risk.

visual.visual_intent: A hand signing a credit application form at a counter, close focus, natural light

scenes.narration: Retailers don't mind. A card that gets declined less means more checkouts completed today.

visual.visual_intent: A busy retail checkout line with customers waiting, motion blur, daylight

scenes.narration: The one-time discount is real. The interest rate is also real, and it outlasts the discount by years if you carry a balance.

visual.visual_intent: Calendar pages flipping forward rapidly, symbolizing time passing, cinematic time-lapse style
visual.decision_reason: visualizes the long-tail cost vs the one-time discount

scenes.narration: The safest way to use one: pay it off before interest ever applies.

visual.visual_intent: A hand tapping a card on a payment terminal, clean close-up, neutral light
